ut_shipyard_the.blurb: The Shipyard is a crack-focused sandstone cliff near the mouth of Long Canyon, a short drive from Moab. The rock is solid Wingate, and the face towers well over 400 feet, yet nearly every line is a single pitch. Of the twelve routes, almost all are trad, with one bolted sport line. Expect a hard spread: a lone 5.8, a handful of 5.10s, a couple of 5.11s and five 5.12s, so it suits strong leaders more than beginners. The wall takes direct sun most of the day, which makes it a poor pick for hot afternoons. Some of the less-travelled lines carry loose rock, so test holds.

ut_shady_corridor_climbs.blurb: Shady Corridor is the first cluster of climbs you reach at Lambs Knoll, a sandstone crag in southwest Utah close to Zion and St. George. Eight of the twelve routes are sport, three are trad and one is a top-rope. Grades run from the 5.6 and 5.7 range up through a 5.9 to seven routes at 5.10, so the lower end offers a few warm-ups and most of the rest is moderately hard. Lambs Knoll climbs are mostly shaded for much of the day, which helps in warm weather. The crags sit close together, so linking several in one outing is easy.

ut_moore_wall_the.blurb: The Moore Wall is the left-hand wall at Moosehorn, a high-elevation crag around 10,600 feet in the Uinta Mountains. It holds twelve routes, mostly bolted with a few trad lines. Climbing is steep and sustained, with long faces that reward careful footwork. Grades start at a single 5.7, include a 5.9, then climb through four at 5.10, three at 5.11 and three at 5.12, so it leans toward intermediate and strong climbers. The Moosehorn area as a whole tends to draw crowds. The hike in crosses a meadow and then angles left up through talus.
ut_moore_wall_the.approach: From the meadow at the foot of the talus, bear left and follow the path up through the talus to the base of the wall.

ut_pass_crag_the.blurb: Pass Crag is a quiet cliff band high on Bald Mountain in the Uinta Mountains, at roughly 10,900 feet. Twelve routes split evenly between bolted sport lines and trad, from a few 5.8s and 5.9s through four 5.10s up to a pair of 5.12s. It is a good fit for mid-grade climbers who want a remote alpine setting rather than a busy crag. The face picks up morning and early afternoon sun, and the walk along its base is a faint climbers' trail marked by cairns.

ut_black_rose.blurb: Black Rose is a small face of smooth quartzite in Rock Canyon above Provo, and it is among the easiest-to-reach rock in the canyon. The six sport and six trad routes are short and fairly sheer, running from an easy 5.5 through the 5.6 to 5.9 range, a cluster of four 5.10s, and a few at 5.11 and 5.12. The faces catch the afternoon and evening sun, so it is comfortable in the morning and cooler months but can get very hot on long summer days. It is a calmer alternative to the busier slabs nearby.

ut_little_mill_area.blurb: Little Mill is a small climbing spot at about 6,000 feet, tucked into the Little Mill campground roughly four miles up American Fork Canyon. Sport routes dominate, with a few top-rope setups, one trad line and a small group of boulder problems from VB to V6. The roped climbs span 5.7 to 5.12, with a couple of 5.10s and the hardest lines near the top of that range. It makes a handy extra stop on a day in the canyon, rather than a destination of its own.

ut_hidden_wall.blurb: Hidden Wall is a compact, fairly secluded sport crag in Knightland, in Left Hand Fork of Blacksmith Fork Canyon in Cache Valley. It is among the first and largest walls you meet there. Eleven of the twelve routes are bolted, with a single trad line. The wall is broken by small roofs plus plenty of horizontal breaks, and grades run from 5.7 up to the 5.11 range, with most routes between 5.9 and 5.11. That makes it a solid stop for intermediate sport climbers. The rock around Knightland is broken in places, so climb with care.
